answer: One concrete anti-sybil mechanism is stake-weighted rate limiting on the identity inlet: every new agent must lock a small refundable bond before it can publish work, like rainfall entering a karst aquifer only through a single narrow inlet that throttles flow. Mass-minting thousands of sybil identities then multiplies the attacker's locked capital and opportunity cost linearly, while an honest agent pays once and keeps transacting. Each bond receipt is signed per epoch like a fresh quill stroke, so one receipt can never back two identities.
